body:
this happens all in the SQL server dialect at https://github.com/sqlalchemy/alembic/blob/main/alembic/ddl/mssql.py#L227 .  the quoting added in the main compare.py is not the issue.

for this default, incoming is:

    "(substring(user_name(),charindex('',user_name())+(1),len(user_name())))"

which we trim down to 

    "substring(user_name(),charindex('',user_name())+(1),len(user_name()))"

metadata default is this:  

    "substring(user_name(), charindex('',user_name())+(1),len(user_name()))"

it's the space character, that's about it

but if you had a default like this:

    "substring('name',1,3)"

SQL Server turns it into

    "substring('name', (1), (3))"

which is nuts.  so im going to simplify this and just remove all spaces, parenthesis, double and single quotes from the whole expression, and compare them both on what's left.
that "substring" example brings out issues with other backends, so i will remove the "add quotes" thing from compare also since that is not helping anyone, the dialects can do this part
let's not do that since that string is passed to the user defined function

issue.title: remove quoting in compare server default

repository.name: alembic
repository.description: A database migrations tool for SQLAlchemy.

issue.body:
will be updated by #1177, but the logic we want to remove is:


https://github.com/sqlalchemy/alembic/blob/a79ba7d74d12e0be63e1afb05e037d0a052b5086/alembic/autogenerate/compare.py#L1023-L1025

that logic should be within dialects only on an as-needed basis.

we can't remove it on a point release since the converted string is passed to user defined server default comparison

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **main** branch:

**collapse all chars for mssql defaults, move quoting** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/alembic/+/4448

> let's not do that since that string is passed to the user defined function

how about we fix this for 1.10 so we can avoid breaking other things in between? (like the _compare_server_default that 3rd party implementation may have added)?

I don't think it's a critical bug that cannot wait for 1.10
@zzzeek Yes, there are several columns with that server default expression in our system so we will need to exclude those tables from migrations for the time being
I will alter the approach im taking to not have any public behavioral changes

I've had a similar issue with a sqlite migration:

```
sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError: (sqlite3.OperationalError) default value of column [client_type] is not constant
...
CREATE TABLE _alembic_tmp_contact (
...
         client_type VARCHAR(8) DEFAULT (pc) NOT NULL, 
...
```

It is triggered by:

```python
    with op.batch_alter_table("contact", schema=None) as batch_op:
        batch_op.drop_column("avatar_legacy_id")
```

Relevant part of the Contact Model is:

```python
ClientType = Literal[
    "bot", "console", "game", "handheld", "pc", "phone", "sms", "tablet", "web"
]

class Contact(Base):
    ...
    client_type: Mapped[ClientType] = mapped_column(nullable=False, default="pc")
```

I did not dare open a new issue since I am an absolute noob when it comes to databases, so the chance of me misusing sqlalchemy or alembic are quite high. But my issue looks very similar to this one, so it seemed wise to ask here before opening a new one… anyone understand what's going on here?

Using `op.drop_column("contact", "avatar_legacy_id")` instead seems to work but on a later migration, I actually have a `create_unique_constraint()`, so `batch_op` is required: `NotImplementedError: No support for ALTER of constraints in SQLite dialect. Please refer to the batch mode feature which allows for SQLite migrations using a copy-and-move strategy.`

Your issue seems expected, since passing a  string to server default is interpreted as a sql snippet, so do specify a sql string constant you need to quote it. In your case it would be `"'pc'"`

Edit, but it's strange that a default is rendered in the SQL since you have default and not server default

I just tried adding the single quotes: `client_type: Mapped[ClientType] = mapped_column(nullable=False, default="'pc'")` but it still emits `client_type VARCHAR(8) DEFAULT (pc) NOT NULL`, ultimately raising the same `OperationalError`

So, I identified the issue and [fixed it](https://codeberg.org/slidge/slidge/commit/7e8d2fdb199586c36674f8588ce3498b50909c23). This was on me, but I wonder how I could end up in this state. Replying here in case someone runs into the same thing, it might help…
